Let it be a sign of your awareness that the person on the other side is a universe unto themselves, worthy of your attention, your respect, and your presence.

the way the corners looked

As we move deeper into a century defined by Artificial Intelligence and automated communication, the act of saying "hello" becomes a radical act of human authenticity. An AI can generate a greeting; it can simulate warmth; it can even pass a Turing test. But an AI cannot *mean* a greeting. It cannot experience the vulnerability of reaching out or the relief of being seen.

The challenge for humanity in the coming decades is to reclaim the "hello." We must ensure that our interactions remain grounded in the reality of human experience. We must continue to look one another in the eye, to use the tone of our voices to convey depth, and to respect the space we create when we choose to speak.

We must teach the next generation that "hello" is not just a habit or a social tic. It is a declaration of peace. It is the fundamental unit of our social contract. It is the recognition that, in the immense, cold silence of the universe, we are not alone. We have each other. And the first step toward building anything meaningful—a friendship, a company, a community, a civilization—is the humble, courageous, and transformative act of saying "hello."

### The Unending Dialogue

Consider, for a moment, the cumulative impact of a single life. If you were to count every "hello" you have uttered in your lifetime, the number would likely be in the hundreds of thousands. Each one was a tiny spark. Some of those sparks caught fire, leading to deep, lifelong bonds. Others flickered out, vanishing into the ether. Yet, every single one contributed to the shape of your reality. You are the sum of your greetings. You are the collection of people you have chosen to acknowledge.

If we view life through this lens, our responsibility becomes clear: to greet with intent. To make our "hellos" count. To be aware of the power we hold when we open our mouths to acknowledge another person. 

The next time you find yourself in an elevator, walking down a quiet hallway, or joining a digital chat, remember the weight of that word. Don't just say it—embody it. Let it be a reflection of your commitment to the human collective. Let it be a sign of your awareness that the person on the other side is a universe unto themselves, worthy of your attention, your respect, and your presence.

In the end, we are all just walking each other home, and the path is paved with these small, luminous exchanges. We greet to remember that we are connected, and we greet to ensure that when we eventually reach the end of our journey, we do not do so as strangers. We are a species defined by our reach—our reach toward the unknown, toward the future, and most importantly, toward one another.

So, let us greet. Let us break the silence. Let us use the two most powerful syllables in any language to build a world where "hello" is not merely the start of a conversation, but the foundation of a life well-lived. Let the greeting be your signature, your promise, and your bridge. 

The world is waiting. The void is vast. The silence is heavy. Speak into it. Say "hello." Begin the work of being human again, one interaction at a time. It is a small thing, perhaps, but it is the only thing that truly holds the architecture of our world together. From the first word of a child to the last words of the aged, the story of humanity is a story of greetings—a long, beautiful, and unending dialogue that begins with the courage to say, "I am here, and I see that you are, too."
